segments.text: July 28, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Angela Boban

criticized the conduct and purpose of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, asserting that its activities create fear and harm within communities and may affect individuals based on their perceived immigration status. She urged American Fork City to adopt an executive order or formal resolution prohibiting federal agents from using City-owned schools, parks, libraries, and public buildings for immigration-enforcement activities and called for ICE to be abolished.
View minutes, page 2
July 28, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Daniel Sroka

reminded City officials and police officers of their oaths to uphold the Constitution and argued that they had a responsibility to address alleged misconduct within the Police Department. He stated that this was his fourth Council meeting and that he had not received a city response regarding concerns he previously raised. He urged residents who had experienced or witnessed alleged police misconduct to attend the August 11 Council meeting, exercise their right to speak, and hold the City accountable.
View minutes, page 2
July 28, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Greg Hazard

expressed opposition to Officer Bronson Kitchen continuing to serve as the school resource officer at American Fork Junior High School. Citing incidents that he characterized as involving aggression, retaliation, and failures to follow safety protocols, Mr. Hazard questioned whether Officer Kitchen was an appropriate example for students and raised concerns about student safety and potential City liability. He urged the city to reevaluate the assignment and inform parents so they could make informed decisions regarding their children.
View minutes, page 2
July 28, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Jan Chamberlain

asked City leaders and the Police Department to cooperate with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement only when agents present a warrant signed by a judge.

She expressed concern about immigration-enforcement practices, emphasized the importance of protecting all people, and stated that immigrants should be properly vetted while retaining their legal right to seek asylum through lawful processes.
View minutes, pages 2–3
July 28, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Kambria Wong

, a lifelong American Fork resident and criminal justice graduate who works with incarcerated youth, discussed her personal connection to immigrant families as the child of an immigrant. She expressed appreciation that the American Fork Police Department had not used its facilities for federal immigration enforcement and asked the City Council to consider a formal resolution or executive action prohibiting federal immigration agents from using City-or county-owned properties for enforcement activities. She emphasized that all residents should feel safe in the community and requested an opportunity to discuss the proposal further with City representatives.

Mayor Frost asked whom Ms. Wong believed would be the most appropriate City representative to meet with and offered to meet with her personally to discuss the proposal. He asked Ms. Wong to complete a contact form so that they could arrange a meeting to discuss her concerns.
